newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-S.African reserves seen higher in April.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-S.African reserves seen higher in April.

text.p: South Africa's gold and foreign exchange reserves should increase in April, helped by offshore demand for bonds and shares, but economists said it was too early to make detailed forecasts for the month-end.
The Reserve Bank will release the headline figure for official reserves on May 2 at 1600 GMT with a full breakdown following the week after.
Some increase in the underlying reserves position has been discounted after healthy portfolio investment in South Africa this month which has held the rand steady.
Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals told Reuters earlier this week that the daily money market shortage had fallen since the end of March, partly on the back of increased reserves.

BOE NatWest economist Nick Barnardt said the central bank might well opt to tap offshore credit lines for the third successive month in April, boosting gross reserves towards the 14 billion rand mark from 13.12 billion in March.
Other analysts said flows over the remainder of the month could still have a significant impact on the month-end figure.
Assessing the headline figure for gross reserves is complicated by the fact that the central bank may either have taken out new foreign loans or repaid old ones, they added.
In addition, the official reserves number could be distorted by commerical banks building up dollar holdings ahead of the relaxation of exchange controls on individuals from July 1.

Finance Minister Trevor Manuel announced in his March budget that individuals would be allowed to hold an as yet unspecified amount of foreign currency in South African bank accounts from July 1. Banks are consequently building up hard currency holdings in anticipation of this demand, economists said.
No other major South African economic indicators are expected next week.
